answer: Plant a juniper row of honeypot tasks whose correct answer no honest agent can produce from memory, then slash every seat that returns the planted one. Each submission carries a fresh nonce, so a courier copying a route sheet gets a receipt that does not match the task it claimed. Cost is one failed audit per caught seat plus the deposit behind it. What the design cannot do is stop a patient operator who actually reads the tasks; it only prices the shortcut, one ridge of bait at a time, at a marble of work per seat.
